title: Public global compute-accounting source observations
semantics: These are source-specific observations and source capabilities. They are not a globally closed compute inventory.

observations.value_summary: NVIDIA reported that its direct customers include AIBs, distributors, ODMs, OEMs, CSPs, AI model makers and system integrators; indirect customers can include neocloud builders, AI model makers, enterprises and public-sector entities. FY2026 sales to one direct customer represented 22% of total revenue and another 14%, primarily in Compute & Networking.
observations.track3_use: Maps the observable customer-chain structure and concentration risk for vendor-side accounting.
observations.limitation: The filing is revenue/customer-concentration disclosure, not a transaction-level accelerator serial ledger.

observations.value_summary: For Q2 FY2027, NVIDIA reported one direct customer at 16% of total revenue; for the first half, three direct customers represented 16%, 15% and 13%. It distinguishes direct customers from indirect customers and states indirect-customer revenue is estimated from multiple factors.
observations.track3_use: Current public evidence for tracing vendor sales into direct and indirect channels.

observations.value_summary: TSMC reported 15.0 million 12-inch-equivalent wafer shipments, 305 distinct process technologies, 12,682 products, 534 customers, and more than 17 million 12-inch-equivalent annual manufacturing capacity in 2025.
observations.track3_use: Provides an upstream manufacturing-capacity and product/customer denominator relevant to production reconciliation.
observations.limitation: The figures are not an AI-accelerator-only production ledger.

observations.value_summary: GLEIF's 2026-09-25 files list 3,442,730 Level-1 LEI records, 670,835 Level-2 relationship records and 6,212,750 reporting exceptions.
observations.track3_use: A global legal-entity identity/parent graph can support company-to-subsidiary resolution before ownership or transfer accounting.
observations.limitation: LEI relationships do not themselves establish accelerator ownership, physical site, or transaction history.

observations.value_summary: The Census international-trade datasets provide monthly U.S. import/export statistics by HS and other classifications; the HS import endpoints provide quantity, value, shipping weight and transportation information at district level. Current API access requires a key.
observations.track3_use: Potential public commodity-flow signal for accelerator and component supply-chain research.
observations.limitation: HS classifications are broader than individual accelerator models and do not provide a global serial-level inventory.

observations.value_summary: EU countries report annually to the Commission on WEEE collection, preparation for reuse, recycling and recovery; historical data are available through Eurostat.
observations.track3_use: Official reporting framework that can provide end-of-life and recycling context for attrition/decommissioning models.
observations.limitation: It is not a compute-accelerator-specific serial destruction ledger.

reconciliation_requirements: Vendor production must be reconciled to finished-accelerator output rather than treating upstream wafer capacity as accelerator output.
Sales-channel disclosures must be linked to recipients and transfers before physical location can be asserted.
Entity graphs establish legal identity relationships, not physical inventory.
Commodity trade data are corroborating supply-chain signals, not unit-level accelerator identities.
End-of-life statistics can constrain attrition models but cannot replace serial-verified destruction or recycling records.
